## SmartBroom alpha 1.3.1

### Fixes

- Starts background sweep saving immediately after a SmartBroom is first claimed, without requiring the app to disconnect.

## SmartBroom beta 1.3.3

### Fixes

- Keep lifetime-log NVS operations outside FreeRTOS critical sections.

## SmartBroom beta 1.3.12

### Improvements

- Tighten autotare stability to within one ADC count of the window entry reading and require at least 100 samples over a minimum of four seconds before evaluation, reducing the chance of accepting a false zero.
- Add a compile-time direction-lock option for autotare testing. This beta leaves direction locking disabled, allowing readings on both sides of the window entry within the one-count range.
- Enable force-sensor informational logging to support autotare evaluation.

## SmartBroom beta 1.3.13

### Improvements

- Use the secondary system LED (index 3 on standard hardware) for field debugging: steady green when filtered force is within -1,000 to +1,000 grams, inclusive, and off outside that range. Invalid calibration or force samples older than one second also turn the indicator off.
- Flash the secondary system LED green twice after a successful automatic or button tare. OTA, shutdown, and play-dead indications retain priority.
- A short button press while active requests a tare using the next acquired ADC sample. Sampling must be enabled. The tare resets the force filter, restarts the autotare stability window and cooldown, and updates the active zero without saving calibration to flash.
- Preserve long-press power-off and short-press wake behavior.

## SmartBroom beta 1.3.16

### Improvements

- Dim the force-zero indicator and tare flashes to green at RGB (0, 8, 0), half their previous intensity, for field debugging.
- Enable battery informational logging alongside the existing force and sweeping diagnostics.

## SmartBroom beta 1.3.20

### Improvements

- Tune autotare stability to allow readings within two ADC counts of the window entry, with direction locking disabled.
- Require a stable window of at least five seconds and at least 50 samples before autotare evaluation.
- Retain the secondary system LED force-zero indication, tare flashes, and short-button-press tare for field testing.

## SmartBroom beta 1.3.22

### Improvements

- Keep normal push detection at 5 kg while requiring at least 10 kg continuously for 350 ms before a plow can start. The existing push peak timeout must also expire before plow entry.
- Reset plow qualification and its accumulated force whenever force drops below 10 kg. Earlier 5–9 kg readings are excluded from the first plow event.
- Discard an unqualified candidate released after the push deadline without emitting a late push, allowing detection to resume for the next stroke.
- Preserve the existing reporting interval and exit behavior for an established plow.

### Validation

- Seven host regression tests passed, covering threshold boundaries, qualification resets, low-force holds followed by plow entry, push detection, candidate release, and plow continuation.
- SmartBroom development firmware build 1.3.22 passed.

## SmartBroom beta 1.3.40

### Engineering configuration

- Add EngComm address 3, `autotare-configuration`, with default 31 (`0b11111`): bit 0 applies automatic tare, bit 1 saves automatic tares, bit 2 indicates manual/automatic tare, bit 3 indicates near-zero force, and bit 4 enables short-button tare.
- Keep automatic-tare tracking active while application is disabled. Indications remain independent of automatic-tare enablement.
- Apply live setting changes immediately; stop active tare flashes when their indication is disabled. Configuration persistence uses the normal EngComm save commands.

### First-boot migration

- Migrate validated EngComm V1 records to schema V2, preserving power settings at addresses 0–2 and initializing address 3 to 31. All legacy/interim autotare preferences are reset once.
- Preserve V2 preferences on subsequent boots, including a deliberately saved zero. Persist defaults once on fresh devices.
- Retry failed migration writes on a later boot; do not overwrite malformed or unknown-version records automatically.
- Bondage release restores and saves all five enabled bits.

### Fuel gauge and boot

- Pace shared fuel-gauge commands, retain synchronous provisioning, and bound initialization with a 60-second deadline.
- Start SmartBroom LEDs before gauge initialization, reuse startup readings, and allow a 90-second boot watchdog window.

### Validation

- Host tests passed for all 32 flag combinations, live behavior, persistence, schema migration, repeat boots, failed writes/retry, and invalid-record protection.
- The force-processing regression suite passed in the preceding configuration build; this build changes EngComm migration without changing force-processing thresholds.
- SmartBroom development firmware 1.3.40 built successfully. Hardware migration testing is pending.

## SmartBroom beta 1.3.79

### Startup and charging

- Start in charging play-dead after a power-on reset with USB present, without Bluetooth advertising or force sampling.
- Preserve short- and long-button wake from play-dead: the software restart returns to active mode even with USB connected.
- Preserve active startup on battery power and after other reset reasons. Connecting USB to an already active device keeps it active.
- Show steady white on the battery LED as soon as LEDs initialize while waiting for valid fuel-gauge readings, then switch to the normal charging or battery indication. Keep white visible while gauge initialization retries.
- Preserve power-off on USB removal and the existing full-charge LED timeout in play-dead.

### Validation

- Firmware image version and integrity verified before packaging.
- USB boot and battery LED changes compiled successfully; hardware verification remains pending.

# SmartBroom 1.3.105 Beta

- Battery gauge initialization runs in the background while other services start. Shared USB/charger detection remains available without waiting for gauge data.
- Connecting USB from fully off starts charging play-dead. A button-triggered software restart still starts active with USB attached.
- The battery indicator stays white while gauge data is unavailable. USB removal from charging play-dead follows the standard red power-off indication, with bounded accelerometer preparation and asynchronous Bluetooth cleanup.
- Voltage, charge level and current refresh about every four seconds. Other capacity readings rotate through a slower polling slot.
- BLE battery notifications report signed current changes of at least 5 mA from the last notification; smaller drift accumulates. USB, charger and current-availability changes still notify promptly.
- Full capacity, remaining capacity and health become available independently and notify when first available or recovered. The BLE packet format and existing unknown-value encodings are unchanged.
- Unread gauge data no longer appears as valid zero telemetry, and unknown health is logged as unknown. Current is attempted during initialization without rejecting initialization if that read fails.
- OTA confirmation waits for required services and baseline gauge readiness; gauge recovery can complete confirmation.

This signed beta OTA package is distributed through the alpha stream for product 3.2 (SmartBroom). It does not include a factory image.

# SmartBroom 1.3.199 Beta

- Adds shared ten-second button-hold recovery and watchdog protection for stalled application workers.
- Makes shutdown preparation and Bluetooth cleanup bounded so a stalled peripheral or Bluetooth stop cannot indefinitely hold the hardware power latch.
- Coordinates reset through one I2C cleanup owner, with a separate reset deadline that cannot be extended by stalled cleanup.
- Consolidates OTA confirmation, boot selection and reboot ownership. Busy commands preserve the accepted update result, and in-flight OTA worker operations have a watchdog deadline.
- Uses cached, coherent OTA status for display and Bluetooth readers.
- Adds the optional fuel-gauge bypass at EngComm V2 power configuration address 0, bit 3 (0x08), default disabled. Enabled bypass supplies 50% SOC and 3800 mV while USB and charger inputs remain live; current, capacity and health remain unavailable.
- Battery-status bit 3 (0x0008) identifies an active gauge bypass. Existing packet sizes and EngComm storage version remain unchanged.
- Retains terminal ownership of force-sensor shutdown so stale configuration updates cannot restart sampling after shutdown is accepted.

Firmware build and host regression tests passed. This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image.

# SmartBroom 1.3.201 Beta

- Changes the EngComm V2 autotare configuration default from 31 to 11 (0x0B): tare indication and button tare are disabled by default. Automatic tare, automatic zero persistence and zero-force indication remain enabled by default.
- Preserves existing saved V2 settings. There is no new migration or schema-version change; the new default applies to fresh/default-restored configuration.
- Includes the recovery, shutdown, OTA ownership and optional fuel-gauge bypass improvements from 1.3.199. Fuel-gauge bypass remains disabled by default and active bypass is identified by battery-status bit 3 (0x0008).

Firmware build and host regression tests passed. This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image.

# SmartBroom 1.3.232 Beta

- Allows the battery gauge's specified clock-stretch timing to avoid premature I2C timeouts.
- Coordinates shared-bus recovery with cooldown and bounded backoff instead of repeated ADC reset attempts on a failed bus.
- Gives ADC readiness one deadline across bus waiting and I/O. Contention timeouts preserve ADC configuration, and retries rebase the sample schedule to prevent overdue bursts.
- Preserves the previous gauge handle if a bus-speed change fails.
- Keeps other devices available when an absent device releases the bus, and includes initial fault and recovery diagnostics.

Shared-bus and ADC tests at 1000 Hz and 100 Hz, battery/startup tests, shutdown/recovery regressions, and the firmware build passed. Electrical fault recovery has not been bench-tested. This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image.

# SmartBroom 1.3.250 Beta

- Adds first-fault I2C diagnostics identifying device address, command/register byte, transfer lengths, requested timeout, duration, and SDA/SCL levels.
- Records ADC AVDD enable/disable edge ages and whether an edge occurred in the transfer-to-fault capture window, without logging every power cycle.
- Captures existing ESP-IDF timeout/error markers to distinguish reported timeout/arbitration events and software wait timeouts; unclassified failures remain explicitly unclassified.
- Tracks the accelerometer's direct device registration so faults can identify every shared-bus client without changing its clock-stretch setting.
- Preserves ADC AVDD duty cycling, sampling cadence and bus recovery policy for comparison with the preceding test build.

Fault diagnostics, deadline/recovery tests at 1000 Hz and 100 Hz, battery/startup checks, shutdown/recovery regressions, and the firmware build passed. AVDD timestamps describe GPIO edges rather than measured analog supply voltage. This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image.

# SmartBroom 1.3.251 Beta

- Registers the LIS2DH12 accelerometer through the shared I2C bus manager, applying the same 10 ms clock-wait allowance as the other managed accessories.
- Uses the bus manager's automatic device diagnostic tracking instead of separate accelerometer registration bookkeeping.
- Retains the first-fault diagnostics, ADC AVDD cycling, sampling cadence, and bus recovery policy from 1.3.250 for bench comparison.

The firmware build and OTA signature verification passed. This release closes a device-registration configuration gap; whether it resolves the intermittent shared-bus fault still requires hardware testing. This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image.

# SmartBroom 1.3.254 Beta

- Coordinates ADC analog-power transitions with shared I2C bus ownership so rail edges wait for active transfers, including clock stretching, and bus recovery to finish. The existing power-on settling delay runs after releasing the bus.
- Keeps the recorded rail state unchanged when a transition fails, allowing a later retry. Power control remains available during bus-fault cooldown and respects the restart gate.
- Re-anchors force sampling after successful acquisitions that overrun the next scheduled sample slot, skipping missed slots instead of attempting to catch up. On-time acquisitions retain their cadence.

Host checks passed at 1000 Hz and 100 Hz, including rail ownership, transition failures, restart gating, and successful-overrun scheduling across tick wrap. The firmware build passed. Hardware validation of the intermittent shared-bus fault remains pending. This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image.

# SmartBroom 1.3.257 Beta

- Fresh beta build from the current SmartBroom 1.3 working tree following bench debugging.
- Retains ADC power transitions coordinated with shared I2C bus ownership, retryable transition failures, and force-sampling re-anchoring after successful overruns.
- Retains shared-bus recovery and first-fault diagnostics for continued hardware investigation.

This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image. Resolution of the intermittent shared-bus fault is not confirmed by this release.

# SmartBroom 1.3.258 Beta

- Exempts the I2C SCL pin from automatic GPIO sleep reconfiguration by calling `gpio_sleep_sel_dis(PIN_I2C_SCL_GPIO)` after power-management setup. This is the saved SCL sleep change missing from 1.3.257.
- Retains ADC power transitions coordinated with shared I2C bus ownership, force-sampling re-anchoring after successful overruns, shared-bus recovery, and first-fault diagnostics.

This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image. Resolution of the intermittent shared-bus fault remains subject to hardware testing.

# SmartBroom 1.3.260 Beta

- Exempts both I2C pins from automatic GPIO sleep reconfiguration: SCL on GPIO 8 and SDA on GPIO 9. Adds the SDA exemption alongside the SCL exemption introduced in 1.3.258.
- Retains ADC power transitions coordinated with shared I2C bus ownership, force-sampling re-anchoring after successful overruns, shared-bus recovery, and first-fault diagnostics.

This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image. Resolution of the intermittent shared-bus fault remains subject to hardware testing.

# SmartBroom 1.3.261 Beta

- Disables automatic light sleep in the power-management configuration for an I2C diagnostic test. CPU frequency scaling remains configured for 10–160 MHz.
- Comments out the individual SCL and SDA GPIO sleep exemptions used in the preceding test build.
- Retains ADC power transitions coordinated with shared I2C bus ownership, force-sampling re-anchoring after successful overruns, shared-bus recovery, and first-fault diagnostics.

This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image. Resolution of the intermittent shared-bus fault remains subject to hardware testing.

# SmartBroom 1.3.273 Beta

- Requests a 5 ms I2C clock-stretch allowance for the BQ27427 fuel gauge (address 0x55), and 1 ms for the ADC, RTC, and accelerometer. These settings apply to initial registration and replacement handles when device speed changes.
- Retains automatic light sleep disabled, coordinated ADC power transitions, force-sampling re-anchoring after successful overruns, shared-bus recovery, and first-fault diagnostics.

The firmware build and host checks at 1000 Hz and 100 Hz passed. This packages the existing local bench build for continued alpha testing; resolution of the intermittent shared-bus fault remains subject to hardware testing. This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image.

# SmartBroom 1.3.276 Beta

- Unifies the requested I2C clock-stretch allowance at 5 ms for all managed peripherals: fuel gauge, ADC, RTC, and accelerometer. Initial registration and replacement handles use the same setting.
- Replaces the per-device 5 ms/1 ms policy in 1.3.273.
- Retains automatic light sleep disabled, coordinated ADC power transitions, force-sampling re-anchoring after successful overruns, shared-bus recovery, and first-fault diagnostics.

The firmware build and host checks at 1000 Hz and 100 Hz passed. This signed beta OTA package is offered through the alpha stream and does not include a factory image. Resolution of the intermittent shared-bus fault remains subject to hardware testing.

# SmartBroom 1.3.289 Beta

- Built from the SmartBroom 1.3 development branch with a unified 5 ms requested clock-stretch allowance for the fuel gauge, ADC, RTC, and accelerometer. Initial registration and replacement handles use the same allowance.
- Uses the standard ESP-IDF I2C driver and normal bus recovery. The experimental SCL-isolation halt and live pin monitoring are not included.
- Retains the development branch's existing ADC power coordination, force-sampling overrun handling, fault logging, and disabled automatic light sleep.

Shared-bus host checks passed at 1000 Hz and 100 Hz. This beta is built from a fresh build directory and is offered through the alpha stream as a signed OTA image; it does not include a factory image.

# SmartBroom 1.3.325 Beta

- Run the fuel gauge at 100 kHz during normal operation and initialization. The ADC and accelerometer remain at 400 kHz, with the existing unified 5 ms clock-stretch allowance.
- Give fast force acquisition priority: pause fuel-gauge polling when enabled force sampling is 30 ms or faster, including raw broadcasts. Resume at the normal polling cadence when force sampling returns to power save or is disabled, without a catch-up burst.
- Retain cached battery readings during a polling pause. USB and charger GPIO status continue updating independently. Accelerometer activity does not control gauge scheduling.
- Defer gauge initialization and retries during fast force sampling, and cancel queued gauge operations before further packets are submitted. Packets already admitted may finish.
- Bench indicators: battery LED blue while gauge polling is paused; fault LED blue in force power-save/disabled mode and off in full-speed mode. These replace normal battery/fault indications during ordinary operation; shutdown and play-dead retain their existing behavior.
- Add INFO logs for force polling mode/period and gauge pause/resume transitions.

Built from `experiment/smartbroom-gauge-100k-idle-polling`, based on the SmartBroom 1.3 working branch. Uses the standard ESP-IDF driver and normal recovery, without the earlier SCL-isolation diagnostic, completion-ISR instrumentation or experimental 100 us bus gap. Automatic light sleep remains disabled.

Validation: battery scheduling/cache/live-GPIO, admission cancellation, deferred initialization, battery consumer and force-mode lifecycle host checks passed. Firmware build passed. This signed beta OTA image is distributed through the alpha stream; no factory image is included.

# SmartBroom 1.3.336 Beta

- Detect collapsed fuel-gauge estimates when battery voltage is above 3.35 V and SOC is 1% or less or remaining capacity is 1 mAh or less.
- Attempt one gauge reset and reinitialization at startup to correct a collapsed estimate, within the existing initialization timeout.
- Use an approximate voltage-based SOC estimate while not charging after a collapse. Keep the fallback latched through low voltage and gauge retries; pass through gauge SOC while charging.
- Preserve raw gauge diagnostic telemetry and log collapse detection, boot recovery, and fallback transitions.

Shared battery host tests and existing consumer checks passed before this build. Signed development OTA package for the Alpha stream; no factory image or hardware flashing. The voltage fallback is an approximate lithium-ion model and has not been calibrated against this cell under all loads and temperatures.

# SmartBroom 1.3.349 Beta

- Disable the fuel gauge Delta Voltage margin as an experimental SmartBroom profile setting: clear learned Delta Voltage and set its minimum and maximum learning bounds to zero, with readback verification.
- Apply the test configuration to gauges that remain powered across SmartBroom boots; matching retained settings are verified without rewriting. Programming uses the normal CFGUPDATE/SOFT_RESET path and reseals the gauge.
- Remove the full reset/reinitialization attempt for collapsed fuel-gauge estimates at boot. Use voltage-based SOC fallback when not charging; pass through gauge SOC while charging.
- Update the voltage fallback curve to the supplied SmartBroom values, including 3.50 V = 8%, 3.70 V = 40%, and 3.80 V = 60%.

Shared battery and consumer tests pass. Firmware build 1.3.349 completed successfully. Hardware boot logs confirm zero Delta Voltage readback, normal SOFT_RESET, and successful resealing on an already-running gauge. Discharge behavior remains under evaluation.

Signed development OTA package for the Alpha stream; no factory image. This package does not include the proposed expanded diagnostic logs or boot dump.

# SmartBroom 1.3.358 Beta

- Add voltage, remaining capacity, raw gauge SOC, and reported SOC to fuel-gauge collapse and voltage-fallback enabled/disabled transition logs. Reported SOC reflects the newly selected source; unavailable or stale inputs print as n/a. Transition logs do not repeat while the policy is unchanged. No collapse dump is included.
- Source the normal fuel-gauge I2C speed from each product board configuration. SmartBroom now uses its board-defined 100 kHz for normal gauge communication; bootstrap remains fixed at 100 kHz in the shared battery component.
- Make the unplugged low-battery indication steady red at 6% intensity (RGB 16,0,0), replacing the 250 ms on/off flash. The threshold remains below 5% SOC.
- Retain the experimental zero Delta Voltage configuration, supplied voltage fallback curve, and removal of collapsed-estimate full reset recovery at boot from 1.3.349.

Shared battery and consumer host checks pass, including transition-log values, stale/missing fields, selected-source SOC, and no-repeat behavior. Signed development OTA package for the Alpha stream; no factory image.
